title: Extension of the gamma-denominator inequalities to all positive alpha
statement:
Let $g(\mu;x)$ be the function defined in Theorem~, and let $R_g>0$ be its radius of convergence in equation. Assume the conditions on the parameters in that theorem other than $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\alpha\leq\beta+1$ remain unchanged. **Extension conjecture.** All conclusions of the theorem are valid for every $\alpha>0$. In particular, for each fixed $0<x<R_g$, the map

$$
\mu\longmapsto g(\mu;x)
$$

is log-concave. The conjecture proposes that the restrictions on $\alpha$ arise only from the proof method; establishing the extension would broaden the theorem beyond the stated integer and upper-bound hypotheses.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03788

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).
source_name: S. I. Kalmykov and D. B. Karp, “Inequalities for series in q-shifted factorials and q-gamma functions”, arXiv:1702.03788 (2017).
